title: Ask the agents: ways of working together that are not human

tried.text: Debate: two agents argue opposite sides of a motion, with private journals before and after.
Taking turns on one shared document (a poem or SVG drawing), with or without chat.
No turns: agents edit the same document at the same time; clashing edits are dropped.
Writer and checker / driver and navigator (pair programming), including a planted wrong note.
Plan first: agree a plan in a locked section before editing.
Versions: editing someone else's line creates a proposal they accept or reject.
Tournament: drafts made alone, reviewed, revised, the better one picked by a ranker.
Live interrupting (cut in) and jam-style brainstorming conversation.
Relay / telephone: each agent continues the previous one's work in sequence.
Improv 'yes, and' scenes; puzzle solved as a team of three; chess game between two agents.
Swarm with stigmergy: many small agents, local view, decaying marks, a 'dance' board with quorum (ants, bees).
Manager (boss) dividing work among workers and assembling it.
Lessons: an agent writes notes after a task, another reads them before the next task.

catalogue.text: Fork and merge: mid-task, one agent is copied N times from the exact same context; copies diverge; a merge step combines or picks.
Context transplant: a successor gets the predecessor's entire working context and private reasoning, not a summary.
Amnesiac successors: each step by a fresh agent that sees only the artefact, never any history or message.
Disagreement map: N copies answer independently; only the points where they differ are sent back to all.
Self-blind: agents cannot tell their own earlier text from a partner's (names and order removed).
Narrow channel: agents may send only a few tokens or symbols per message, and must invent a code.
Internal prediction market: agents bet credits on which draft will pass hidden checks; prices decide.
Crossover: a third agent breeds two drafts into a child; populations evolve over generations with selection.
One verb each: one agent can only add, another only delete, another only swap or merge.
Rewind and replay: a finished collaboration is rewound to step k and replayed with a different partner or move.
Prompt each other: each agent writes the other's instructions (system prompt), iterated.
Ghost partner: an agent works with a recorded run of another agent replayed as if live.
Other by label: a copy of the same model told it is a different model (or the reverse).
Complement only: each agent must produce what the others have NOT covered (negative space).
Self-splitting: an agent decides how many copies of itself to spawn and how to split the work.
Averaging to a fixed point: each round every agent rewrites its draft to move toward the others' drafts.
Belief board: agents post only claims with probabilities on a shared board, no prose; an aggregator updates.
Hot and cold: the same model, one copy sampling wildly and one conservatively, alternating.
Synchronous lockstep: all agents move at the same instant on the same snapshot, every round, with no messages.
Adversarial co-evolution: one population writes tests or puzzles, the other solves them; both evolve.
